hints: Focus on the strict rule for hydrogen bonding, it needs H attached directly to N, O or F, not just the presence of those atoms.
Look quickly through the four formulas and spot which one actually contains an O-H group that can donate a hydrogen bond.
Remember that molecules that can both donate and accept can form strong networks that need extra energy to break on boiling.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Condition for Hydrogen Bonding**

Hydrogen bonding between molecules needs H bonded directly to a very electronegative atom. Think N-H, O-H or F-H as the donor.

Rule to check:
$$\text{H-bond donor needed} = \text{H attached to N, O or F}$$

**Test Each Compound for a Donor**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ is an aldehyde with C-H and C=O, but no O-H. $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$ is an ether with C-H and C-O, but no O-H. $\text{HCO}_2\text{CH}_3$ is an ester with C-H and C=O, but no O-H.

Only $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$, methanoic acid, has:
$$\text{H-C(=O)-O-H}$$

**Link Structure to Boiling Point**

The O-H in the carboxylic acid can donate a hydrogen bond, and the C=O can accept. This lets molecules form dimers and extended networks.
Breaking these extra strong intermolecular forces needs more energy, so the boiling point is raised by hydrogen bonding.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, ethanal, is polar due to C=O so has dipole-dipole forces, but it has no O-H, N-H or F-H donor. Many students pick it because it contains oxygen, but oxygen alone without attached H cannot donate a hydrogen bond.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$, dimethyl ether, has an oxygen that can accept a hydrogen bond but no H attached to O to donate one. Pure ether therefore cannot hydrogen bond to itself, so its boiling point is low and controlled by weak van der Waals forces.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{HCO}_2\text{CH}_3$, methyl methanoate, is an ester. It has C=O oxygens that are good acceptors but no O-H donor. Like aldehydes and ethers, it cannot form hydrogen bonds with itself.
options.D: Correct. $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$, methanoic acid, contains the carboxylic acid group $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ with a clear O-H bond. It can donate via O-H and accept via C=O, forming very strong hydrogen-bonded dimers, which greatly raises its boiling point.
